newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Greek farmers' strike jams Bulgarian border.
newsitem.headline: Greek farmers' strike jams Bulgarian border.

text.p: A 12-day blockade by Greek farmers has caused a 2 km traffic jam of cars, trucks and buses on the Bulgarian side of the border, Bulgarian police said on Monday.

"Vehicles have been stuck at the border for more than a week waiting for the lifting of the blockades on Greek territory," said Valentin Tsenev, police officer on duty at the border checkpoint at Kulata, 145 km (90 miles) south of Sofia.
He said truck drivers had been stranded for days with no food and tonnes of perishable products like milk and meat had been ruined.
Tsenev said Bulgarian authorities had held talks with their Greek colleagues last week but they were unable to do anything.
"However, we made a deal for the transit of 10 cars per day," Tsenev said, adding that further talks with the Greek authorities were expected on Monday.
Farmers have staged blockades across Greece to press demands for price supports, cheaper fuel, the rescheduling of $1.3 billion in debts, and lower value added tax on farming equipment.
